X and Y cross-validate strongly on several major findings (stale-drain double-seed bug, unconditional registry override risk, dead async_tokens_to_discard writes, unconditional warmup(), probe_task leak, enforce_eager coverage loss), which is good grounding evidence for both. X loses precision points on claims Y explicitly contradicts (randomize_inputs is validated safe by Y, VLLM_CACHE_ROOT isolation validated safe by Y) plus an unverifiable 'CI gates are red' claim that oversteps a diff-only review. X's fix suggestions include more inline code snippets, giving it a slight actionability edge, but Y's more disciplined validated/confirmed structure and closer topical overlap with the real reviewer give it the overall win.
